title: Advertising Law Compliance in 2026: Five Developments Every Advertiser Should Know | ArentFox Schiff

facts.fact: New York enacted a law requiring advertisers to conspicuously disclose when an ad features a synthetic performer, and the law takes effect June 9.
facts.quote: In 2025, New York enacted a first-in-the-nation law requiring businesses to disclose the use of “synthetic performers”

facts.fact: According to the article, the FTC settled with Growth Cave for $48.6 million over alleged violations, including claims that its AI software would automate 'nearly 100%' of online course building.
facts.quote: the FTC settled with Growth Cave for $48.6 million over a number of alleged violations

facts.fact: The FTC's 'Operation AI Comply' initiative was launched in 2024 to target inflated or unsubstantiated claims about AI capabilities.
facts.quote: The FTC’s “Operation AI Comply” initiative, launched in 2024, made this a sustained enforcement priority.

facts.fact: According to the article, the FTC has brought more than a dozen actions targeting inflated or unsubstantiated claims about AI capabilities since Operation AI Comply began.
facts.quote: Since its inception, the agency has brought more than a dozen actions targeting inflated or unsubstantiated claims about AI capabilities

facts.fact: The NAD recommended changes to an advertiser's claim that its hydrocolloid bandages healed wounds '2x faster'; after the advertiser failed to comply, the matter was referred to the FTC and FDA.
facts.quote: the advertiser, ASO, LLC, claimed that its hydrocolloid bandages healed wounds “2x faster.”

facts.fact: The FTC's Junk Fee Rule took effect in May 2025 and requires advertised prices in live event ticketing and short-term lodging to include all mandatory fees other than reasonable shipping costs and taxes.
facts.quote: The FTC’s Junk Fee Rule, which took effect in May 2025, addresses drip pricing in the live event ticketing and short-term lodging sectors

facts.fact: California's Honest Pricing Law took effect July 1, 2025, applying all-in pricing requirements across industries.
Minnesota's all-in pricing statute took effect January 1, 2025.
New York's Algorithmic Pricing Disclosure Act, targeting surveillance pricing, took effect November 10, 2025, and requires a clear and conspicuous disclosure with statutorily mandated wording.
facts.quote: which took effect on November 10, 2025. The Algorithmic Pricing Disclosure Act targets “surveillance pricing”

facts.fact: The FTC's Click-to-Cancel rule was vacated by a federal appellate court in July 2025 on procedural grounds before it took effect.
facts.quote: was vacated by a federal appellate court in July 2025 on procedural grounds before it ever took effect.

facts.fact: California's amended Automatic Renewal Law took effect July 1, 2025 and requires express affirmative consent, annual reminders regardless of term length, and a prominent click-to-cancel button.
facts.quote: California’s amended Automatic Renewal Law (effective July 1, 2025) now requires “express affirmative consent”

facts.fact: More than two dozen states have auto-renewal laws on the books.
facts.quote: More than two dozen states now have auto-renewal laws on the books, and the list continues to grow.

facts.fact: The FTC's 2025 action against NextMed alleged the telehealth company used unsubstantiated weight-loss claims, fake testimonials, and manipulated reviews to sell GLP-1-related programs.
facts.quote: Its 2025 action against NextMed alleged that the telehealth company capitalized on GLP-1 demand
